methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update an MCP server resource.

 If the resource doesn't exist, creates it. If it exists, updates it.
 The resource is identified by its (scope, org, slug) combination.

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create an MCP server resource.

 Returns an error if a resource with the same (scope, org, slug) already exists.
 Use `apply` for idempotent create-or-update semantics.

methods.name: Update
methods.description: Update an existing MCP server resource.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete an MCP server resource.

 Permanently removes the MCP server definition.
 Agents referencing this server will need to be updated.

methods.name: UpdateVisibility
methods.description:
Update the visibility of an existing MCP server.

 Only modifies metadata.visibility, leaving spec, status, and other
 metadata fields untouched.

methods.name: Connect
methods.description:
Connect to an MCP server and discover its tools.

 Connects to the MCP server, enumerates tools and resource templates,
 records which tools the server marks destructive, and stores the
 results in status.discovered_capabilities.
 Blocks until the operation settles — legitimately minutes for heavy
 stdio servers (the server-side workflow ceiling is the bound) — and
 returns the updated McpServer.

 Prefer startConnect for interactive clients: browsers can drop a
 no-bytes-yet unary response around ~300s, below the workflow ceiling,
 so a blocking connect can appear to fail while succeeding server-side.
 This RPC remains for callers that want synchronous semantics (and for
 backends that do not yet serve startConnect).

methods.name: StartConnect
methods.description:
Start a connect operation without waiting for it: discovery runs
 server-side, and the caller observes progress by
 polling the resource.

 Returns the McpServer immediately with status.connect_status describing
 the accepted operation (phase CONNECTING, plus a warning when no runner
 appears to be polling the task queue). Poll get/getByReference until
 status.connect_status reaches a terminal phase; results land in
 status.discovered_capabilities exactly as with the blocking connect.

 Idempotent while an operation is in flight: a startConnect that finds a
 live CONNECTING operation attaches to it (the in-flight operation's
 runtime_env wins) instead of starting a second workflow. A CONNECTING
 entry orphaned by a backend restart is reconciled against Temporal
 before a new operation starts.

methods.name: DisconnectOAuth
methods.description:
Disconnect the authenticated user's sign-in for an MCP server.

 Removes the sign-in saved at the server's address in the caller's My
 vault, with its access and refresh tokens. The MCP server definition is
 unchanged. A pasted login at the address is left in place, and so is a
 sign-in saved into a shared vault: the vault's removeConnections removes
 either.

 Idempotent: returns disconnected=true when a sign-in was removed,
 disconnected=false when none was saved. Never returns an error
 for a missing sign-in.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get an MCP server by its unique identifier.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get an MCP server by reference (scope + org + slug).

 Preferred method for looking up MCP servers by name/slug rather than
 system-generated ID.

methods.name: GetOAuthGrantStatus
methods.description:
Check whether the authenticated user has a sign-in for an MCP server in
 their My vault in the specified org: a sign-in saved at the server's
 address, whichever tool or page started it. A pasted login and a
 sign-in saved into a shared vault are read through the vault's own
 RPCs.

 Returns sign-in metadata (connected status, token expiry, auth method)
 without exposing any secret token values. The frontend uses this to
 render the correct OAuth state in the MCP server detail page and
 session composer.

methodTypes.name: UpdateVisibilityInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for updating the visibility of any API resource.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers to change visibility.
 Each controller's updateVisibility RPC accepts this shared input
 and returns the full updated resource.

 Visibility transitions trigger FGA tuple management in Cloud mode. Each
 level maps to exactly one tuple shape; on a transition the tuple for the
 old level is removed and the tuple for the new level is created:
 - PRIVATE:  no visibility tuple (owner + explicit grants only)
 - ORG:      resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

 Not all resources support all visibility levels — the supported set is
 declared per kind via VisibilityConfig in kind_meta:
 - Blueprints (agent, skill, mcp_server, plugin):
     PRIVATE, ORG, or CHILD_ORGS
 - Org-only kinds (vault):
     PRIVATE or ORG (never CHILD_ORGS — tenant isolation)

 visibility_public is refused for every kind (INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the
 supported levels); the level is retired.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource whose visibility is being updated.

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
The new visibility setting for the resource.
 Must not be unspecified (0). Valid values depend on resource kind —
 see the VisibilityConfig in the kind's kind_meta.

methodTypes.name: ConnectInput
methodTypes.description: ConnectInput is the request for the connect RPC.

fields.name: McpServerId
fields.description:
System-generated ID of the MCP server to connect to.
 Obtained from McpServer.metadata.id (e.g., via getByReference).

fields.name: RuntimeEnv
fields.description:
Optional environment variable values for one-time use, ahead of the
 caller's My vault.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context for credential resolution.

 The caller's My vault in this organization is the one connect reads.

 Required: the backend rejects the request when this field is empty.

methodTypes.name: DisconnectOAuthInput
methodTypes.description: DisconnectOAuthInput tears down a user's sign-in for an MCP server.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to disconnect OAuth for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context: the caller's My vault in this org is the one
 changed.

methodTypes.name: DisconnectOAuthOutput
methodTypes.description: DisconnectOAuthOutput reports the result of a disconnect request.

fields.name: Disconnected
fields.description:
Whether a saved sign-in was found and removed.
 true: the connection and its tokens were removed.
 false: no sign-in was saved for this server, org and caller. The desired
 state (no OAuth connection) was already achieved. This is not an error.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, MCP servers and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, MCP_SERVER).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

methodTypes.name: GetOAuthGrantStatusInput
methodTypes.description: GetOAuthGrantStatusInput queries the OAuth grant status for a resource.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to check grant status for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context. Required because the same user can have
 separate OAuth connections for a shared resource across orgs.

methodTypes.name: GetOAuthGrantStatusOutput
methodTypes.description: GetOAuthGrantStatusOutput returns the current OAuth grant status.

fields.name: Connected
fields.description: Whether the user has a sign-in saved at this server's address in this org.

fields.name: AccessTokenExpiresAt
fields.description:
When the access token expires (Unix timestamp seconds).
 0 if no sign-in is saved or the token does not expire.

fields.name: TargetEnvVar
fields.description:
The env var the saved sign-in fills.
 Empty if no sign-in is saved.

fields.name: AuthMethod
fields.description:
Which auth method was used ("mcp_oauth" or "vendor_oauth").
 Empty if no sign-in is saved.

fields.name: ConnectionHealth
fields.description:
Evaluated health of the OAuth connection.
 Provides an actionable signal beyond the binary "connected" field:
 the frontend can distinguish "healthy" from "expired but refreshable"
 from "expired and needs re-auth" from "never connected."

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, agent_share,
 skill, mcp_server), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role SSO auto-provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: iam_policy
values.description: Role-based access control policy for granting permissions on resources.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: identity_provider
values.description: External identity provider for federated authentication.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: platform_client
values.description: OAuth2 client credential for platform builders embedding Stigmer into their products.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: mcp_server
values.description: External tool server connected via the Model Context Protocol.

values.name: agent_share
values.description: Hosted chat link for an agent with its own audience, origins, and credentials.

values.name: agent_channel
values.description: Connection binding an agent to an external messaging platform workspace.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that agent
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: execution_context
values.description: User-owned runtime context for managing execution state.

values.name: schedule
values.description: Recurring trigger that runs an agent on a cron schedule.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: the archive Stigmer materialised into
 skills, MCP servers and an agent, and the handle that upgrades
 and removes them together. A plugin is what you install; an agent is what
 runs. Members are the resources labelled with the plugin's id.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

enumTypes.name: OAuthConnectionHealth
enumTypes.description:
OAuthConnectionHealth evaluates the health of an OAuth connection by
 examining whether a login is saved and its token expiry metadata. Used in
 GetOAuthGrantStatusOutput to give the frontend an actionable signal
 beyond the binary "connected" boolean.

 The backend determines health from locally available metadata (the
 saved connection and its sign-in expiry). It cannot detect server-side token
 revocation without making an API call to the vendor, so HEALTHY means
 "valid as far as we know" — not a guarantee the token will be accepted.

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_HEALTHY
values.description: The access token exists and is not expired (or does not expire).

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED
values.description:
The access token is expired and no refresh token is available.
 The user must re-authenticate via the OAuth flow.

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED_REFRESHABLE
values.description:
The access token is expired but a refresh token is available.
 The backend will attempt automatic refresh at run time.
 If the refresh token is itself expired, the refresh will fail and
 the user will need to re-authenticate.

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_NO_GRANT
values.description:
No sign-in made for this server that a run would use: the user has
 never signed in, has disconnected, or the saved login is not a
 sign-in this server can use.

enumTypes.name: ValidationState
enumTypes.description:
ValidationState represents the structural validity of an MCP server definition.
 This is NOT runtime health — it only indicates whether the definition is valid.

values.name: valid
values.description:
The MCP server definition is structurally valid.
 All required fields are present and have valid values.
 The definition can be referenced by agents.

values.name: invalid
values.description:
The MCP server definition is invalid.
 Check validation_message for details on what's wrong.
 The definition should be corrected before use.

enumTypes.name: ConnectPhase
enumTypes.description:
ConnectPhase is the lifecycle of a connect operation.

 Exactly three phases: one live, two terminal. There is no queued/pending
 distinction — the Temporal workflow is started before CONNECTING is ever
 persisted, so CONNECTING always means "a workflow run exists".

values.name: connect_phase_connecting
values.description:
A connect workflow is running (or was running when the backend last
 observed it — see ConnectStatus.workflow_id for how stale entries are
 reconciled).

values.name: connect_phase_succeeded
values.description:
The connect completed and its results were persisted to
 discovered_capabilities.

values.name: connect_phase_failed
values.description:
The connect settled without usable results. failure_code and
 failure_message carry the same classification the blocking connect RPC
 reports as a gRPC error.

enumTypes.name: VendorApprovalStatus
enumTypes.description:
Lifecycle status of an OAuthApp's vendor marketplace approval.

 Vendors like Slack, Figma, and Salesforce require third-party OAuth
 apps to pass a review/approval process before they can be used by
 end users. This enum tracks that lifecycle.

values.name: VENDOR_APPROVAL_STATUS_PENDING
values.description:
The OAuth app has been submitted to the vendor for review and is
 awaiting approval. The sign-in button is disabled in the UI.

values.name: VENDOR_APPROVAL_STATUS_APPROVED
values.description: The vendor has approved the OAuth app. Sign-in is enabled.

values.name: VENDOR_APPROVAL_STATUS_REJECTED
values.description: The vendor rejected the OAuth app. Sign-in is disabled.

resourceDescription: McpServer represents a reusable MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configuration.

statusType.name: McpServerStatus
statusType.description: McpServerStatus represents the system-managed state of an MCP server definition.

fields.name: ValidationState
fields.description:
Validation state of the MCP server definition.
 Indicates whether the definition passed structural validation.

fields.name: ValidationMessage
fields.description:
Human-readable validation message.
 Populated when validation_state is INVALID to explain what's wrong.
 Empty when validation_state is VALID or UNSPECIFIED.
 Examples:
 - "server_type is required: must specify stdio, http, or docker"
 - "http.url is not a valid URL: missing scheme"
 - "docker.image is required"

fields.name: DiscoveredCapabilities
fields.description:
Tools and resource templates discovered from the MCP server.
 Optional — absent until the connect RPC has been called.

fields.name: OauthStatus
fields.description:
OAuth-related enrichment state, populated at query time by the backend.
 Carries the vendor approval status resolved from the referenced OAuthApp
 (fields 1-2; fields 3-4 are never populated — see OAuthStatus).
 None of these fields are persisted.

fields.name: ConnectStatus
fields.description:
State of the most recent connect (discovery) operation.

 Persisted (unlike oauth_status). Written by the backend when a connect
 operation starts and again when it settles; clients poll it through the
 ordinary get/getByReference queries after startConnect returns.
 Absent until the first connect is attempted.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: PlatformClientId
fields.description:
The PlatformClient whose minted user token the actor acted through.
 Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records no act
 (an account's profile lookup).

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: ConnectStatus
statusNestedTypes.description: ConnectStatus records one connect operation — the most recent one.

fields.name: Phase
fields.description: Where the operation stands. See ConnectPhase.

fields.name: WorkflowId
StartedAt
fields.description: When the operation was accepted (workflow started).

fields.name: FinishedAt
fields.description: When the operation settled (success or failure). Unset while CONNECTING.

fields.name: FailureCode
fields.description:
gRPC status code name classifying the failure, mirroring what the
 blocking connect RPC returns for the same outcome (CamelCase, the Go
 grpc codes.Code String() form):
 - "FailedPrecondition": the target server (or its credentials/config)
   refused the connect with a user-facing message — failure_message
   renders verbatim.
 - "DeadlineExceeded": the workflow run timeout elapsed.
 - "Unavailable": the workflow run disappeared (e.g. Temporal data loss).
 - "Internal": unexpected runner/backend error (failure_message carries
   the runner's classified, user-facing connect-failure text — the same
   deliberate exception the blocking RPC makes, stigmer/stigmer#478).
 Empty unless phase is connect_phase_failed.

fields.name: FailureMessage
fields.description:
Human-readable failure detail. Same rendering contract as the blocking
 connect RPC's error message. Empty unless phase is connect_phase_failed.

fields.name: Warning
fields.description:
Non-fatal advisory recorded at start time, rendered by clients alongside
 the CONNECTING state. Today's only source is the dead-runner pre-flight:
 when no worker is polling the runner task queue at start, this warns
 that the operation may sit unclaimed (deliberately warn-only — a worker
 may be booting, and the pre-flight has a startup false-negative race).
 Empty when the pre-flight saw a live worker.

statusNestedTypes.name: DiscoveredCapabilities
statusNestedTypes.description: DiscoveredCapabilities holds the tools and resource templates reported by an MCP server.

fields.name: Tools
fields.description: Callable tools reported by the MCP server.

fields.name: ResourceTemplates
fields.description: Read-only data endpoints reported by the MCP server.

fields.name: LastDiscoveredAt
fields.description: When this snapshot was captured.

statusNestedTypes.name: DiscoveredResourceTemplate
statusNestedTypes.description: DiscoveredResourceTemplate describes a parameterized resource template reported by an MCP server.

fields.name: UriTemplate
fields.description:
URI template with placeholders (RFC 6570).
 Example: "stigmer://agents/{org}/{slug}"

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Identifier for this resource template.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Human-readable description of the resource.

fields.name: MimeType
fields.description:
MIME type of the resource content.
 Example: "application/json"

statusNestedTypes.name: DiscoveredTool
statusNestedTypes.description: DiscoveredTool describes a single tool reported by an MCP server.

fields.name: Name
fields.description:
Unique tool name within the MCP server (case-sensitive).
 Example: "search", "get_agent", "apply_mcp_server"

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Human-readable description of the tool's purpose.

fields.name: InputSchema
fields.description: JSON Schema describing the tool's input parameters.

fields.name: DestructiveHint
fields.description:
True when the server's own MCP annotation marks the tool destructive
 (annotations.destructiveHint is exactly true), whatever readOnlyHint says.
 A destructive tool asks for approval before it runs. An absent annotation
 reads as false: Stigmer acts only on an explicit declaration, so a server
 that annotates nothing gates nothing.

statusNestedTypes.name: OAuthStatus
statusNestedTypes.description: OAuthStatus holds system-derived OAuth enrichment state for an MCP server.

fields.name: VendorApprovalStatus
fields.description:
Vendor marketplace/app-review approval status of the login app the
 organization keeps for this server's address. Resolved at query time.
 When the app is pending vendor approval, the frontend gates the sign-in
 button and offers pasting a token instead.

fields.name: VendorApprovalDocsUrl
fields.description:
Documentation URL for users while the login app is pending vendor
 approval. Resolved at query time. Empty when the app has no
 documentation link or is already approved.
